sentences.text: Raja Reddy Koneti, Advocate for the Petitioners and of Public Prosecutor for the Respondent, the Court made the following.
ORDER THE HON'BLE SMT JUSTICE LALITHA KANNEGANTI CRIMINAL PETITION No.306 OF 2021 ORDER:-

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.')) to quash the proceedings in F.I.R.No.25 of 2021 dated 13.01.2021 of Tiruvuru Police Station, Krishna District registered for the offences punishable under Sections 270, 273 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C."} and Section 22 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act,
2003 (for short 'COTP Act).
2.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act,
2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners before this Court are Al and A2 in the above said crime.

3. The brief facts of the case are that while the Police were conducting vehicle search two persons came on Hero Splendor Plus Vehicle bearing No.AP 39 DL 7074 from Mallela village and on seeing the Police they tried to escape.
But the Police apprehended them and on questioning they revealed that they have purchased the said products from an unknown lorry driver for the purpose of selling the same at higher prices.
On verification the Police found Blue Bull and other varieties of tobacco products.
Basing on the same the present crime is registered against the petitioners and tobacco products were seized.

4. Heard Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor for the State.
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that Sections 270 and 272 I.P.C. relate to food safety standards.
Section 270 LPC. speaks about malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life and Section 273 of I.P.C. speaks about sale of Noxious Food or Drink.
Neither of the sections is applicable to the present case as tobacco will not spread any infection and it does not fall under the category of food or drink or poison.
Moreover, the Police have no power to register the offences under above Sections except the designated officers like Food Safety Officer.

6, Learned Counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch,
wherein it was held that tobacco does not fall within the definition of "food" as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act.
Therefore, registration of FIR under the above sections is not permissible.

7. The provisions of COTP Act also do not apply to the case on hand as it was held by this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch that the provisions of the COTP Act can only be pressed into service in limited circumstances i.e. when there is violation of Sections 4 to 7 and 10 of the COTP Act.

It is not the case of the prosecution that the petitioners had committed any violation Kunduru Manikanta vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 25 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93308411/
2 of the provisions of COTP Act.

sentences.text: Hence, he submits that in terms of the aforesaid orders, this Criminal Petition may be allowed.
To, DROWN 9, The above submissions are not disputed by learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State.

10. In the light of the aforementioned orders, this criminal petition is allowed and F.I.R.No.25 of 2021 dated 13.01.2021 of Tiruvuru Police Station, Krishna District is hereby quashed against the petitioners.

As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
